shell.cancelTip: Stops the running survey. Changes to the system cannot be cancelled.
shell.dryRunTip: Changes are only logged, never carried out.

start.dryRunActive: Dry run is active. Nothing will be changed.
start.readOnly: This drive is write-protected — logs and reports cannot be saved.
start.settingsReadOnly: The language choice applies to this session only — this drive cannot be written to.
start.dryRunOn: Dry run on — changes are only logged.
start.dryRunOff: Dry run off — changes are carried out for real.
start.languageBusy: '{name}' is still running. The language can only be changed afterwards — switching rebuilds the page, which would not sit well with a survey in progress.
start.fontsMissing: Bundled fonts unavailable, falling back to system fonts.

dialog.busyMessage: '{name}' is still running. Cancelling may leave the system half-changed.
dialog.languageMessage: The interface switches immediately — no restart needed. Values already measured are kept.
dialog.themeFailed: The theme could not be loaded:
dialog.windowFailed: The main window could not be loaded:

ai.title: Copilot, Recall and the rest
ai.lead: Block first, then remove. The blocks also work in advance, in case a feature update brings AI components back.

apps.title: Programs
apps.lead: Installed through winget, Microsoft's package service. Programs can also be downloaded to the drive beforehand so they can be installed later without internet.

unin.title: Remove programs
unin.lead: The same list as in Control Panel. Preinstalled manufacturer software and expired antivirus trials can be removed here in one go — on request completely, including leftover folders and registry keys.
unin.hidden: {anzahl} entries are hidden — please use the search above.
unin.confirmMessage: {anzahl} program(s) will be removed. This cannot be undone — they have to be installed again afterwards.
unin.confirmLoud: {anzahl} of them bring their own wizard and will ask again themselves. WinZii has to wait for that — please click those windows through.
unin.leftoverMessage: {entfernt} removed, {fehlgeschlagen} failed. The uninstallers left things behind ({groesse}). Registry keys are exported to a .reg file before they go. Deleted folders are gone for good — including any settings and profiles inside them.
unin.logStillListed: {name} is still in the program list — not counted as removed.
unin.detailStillListed: still in the program list — cancelled, or a restart is pending
unin.msgNoCommand: no usable uninstall command on record
unin.msgTimeout: the wizard ran into a timeout
unin.detailOutside: not removed — outside the permitted areas
unin.logOutside: Leftover skipped, outside the permitted areas: {pfad}
unin.undoHint: Folders are deleted for good; removed registry keys sit in the backup folder as a .reg file.

core.wearUnknown: Battery present, but reports no capacity
core.logBatteryReport: Battery report could not be read: {grund}
core.placeholderLead: This area is still being built.
core.dialogSkipped: Dialog '{titel}' skipped — the window is already gone.
core.busyLog: A task is already running ({name}). Please wait.
core.busyInfoMessage: “{name}” has not finished yet. Please wait until it is done, then try again.
core.logProtectionOn: System protection for {laufwerk} was off and has been switched on. It stays on — otherwise the restore point would vanish again straight away. This costs some disk space.
core.logProtectionFailed: System protection could not be switched on — a restore point may not be possible.
core.undoMarkFailed: The backup could not be marked as reverted: {grund}

auto.title: What starts when you sign in
auto.lead: Every entry here lengthens startup and uses memory. Disabled entries are kept and can be switched back on at any time — nothing is deleted.
auto.listHint: Click to switch on or off

clean.title: Free up disk space
clean.lead: Analyse first, then choose deliberately. WinZii only ever deletes caches and system leftovers — never your own files.
clean.resultHint: Click “Analyse” to find out how much space is in use.

dash.title: Dashboard
dash.lead: The state of this PC at a glance — the starting point for any service job.
dash.logNoSystemData: System data could not be read.
dash.noGpu: No graphics card could be read.
dash.noMonitor: No display reports in — with remote access that is normal.
dash.serialNone: none on record — normal for a self-build
dash.noticeReboot: A restart is pending ({grund}). Some changes only take effect afterwards.
dash.noticeWriteBlocked: This drive cannot be written to. Log, backups and reports cannot be saved — which means there is no way back from any change. Please switch to a writable drive before changing anything.
dash.noticeFat32: WinZii is running from a FAT32 drive. For Office downloads exFAT or NTFS is recommended (4 GB file limit).
dash.noticeDryRun: Dry run is active: changes are only logged, never carried out.

diag.title: Fault analysis
diag.lead: Event logs, blue screens and drive health — summarised and put into plain language instead of raw data.
diag.reliabilityHint: Crashes, application faults and installations on one timeline. This is where you see whether a problem coincides with an installation — the event list does not show that.

drv.title: Drivers
drv.lead: Devices that are not working — and the driver backup, without which a laptop can easily end up with no Wi-Fi after a fresh install.
drv.devicesHint: Reads Device Manager and puts the error codes into plain language.
drv.tipShowMicrosoft: Microsoft's own drivers are almost always old and perfectly fine all the same.
drv.inventoryHint: Oldest first. With blue screens and crashes the suspect is usually right at the top.
drv.backupTitle: Back up drivers to the drive
drv.backupHint: The backup goes next to WinZii under offline\treiber and can be restored in one go after a fresh install.

off.title: Set up Office
off.lead: Microsoft Office through the official deployment tool — or LibreOffice if there is no licence.
off.keyHint: Without a key Office still installs, but it is not activated. The key is not stored on the drive.
off.libreLead: Free of charge and without a licence key. Also opens and saves the Microsoft Office formats — perfectly sufficient for most private customers.

opt.title: Windows optimisation
opt.lead: Speed, telemetry, privacy and security. Every change is backed up beforehand and can be undone individually.

log.title: Session log
log.lead: Every step is written down — as evidence for the customer and as a reminder for you.
log.outputHint: Reports are stored on the WinZii drive.
log.handoverHint: Sums up in the customer's language what was done, how much space was gained, how the PC is equipped and what is still open. The log above is a developer log and unsuitable for that.

rest.title: Restore
rest.lead: The other half of the data move: whatever was backed up on the data page comes back onto the PC here — Wi-Fi networks, bookmarks, printers and network drives.
rest.sourceHint: The search covers offline\daten. A backup from a different machine can be restored as well — it is then marked as such.
rest.wlanHint: The profiles are created for all users. If the backup was made without keys, the entry is created but the PC will not connect on its own.
rest.bookmarksHint: The existing bookmark file is replaced. WinZii puts a copy ending in .winzii-vorher next to it first. The browser has to be closed.
rest.devicesHint: A printer can only be created if its driver is already installed — otherwise it appears here as a note rather than an error. Protected shares ask for their own credentials.

tool.title: Repair
tool.lead: The moves needed most often day to day — each with an explanation of what actually happens.
tool.checkHint: Checks network adapter, IP address, router, name resolution and internet access one after another — and says which of the buttons below helps.
tool.netHint: Try the quick refresh first. The full reset helps when nothing works at all, and needs a restart.
tool.updateHint: Resets the update cache. The old folders are only renamed, not deleted — Windows recreates them at the next update.
tool.printerHint: For when print jobs are stuck in the queue and cannot be deleted.
tool.defenderHint: A quick scan by Windows Defender. With “the PC is slow”, malware is among the most common causes.
tool.restoreHint: Worth doing before bigger changes. Windows normally allows only one point per day — WinZii lifts that limit briefly.
tool.bloatHint: Apps that come with Windows and only take up space on most customer machines.

data.title: Data
data.lead: The question before every fresh install: what needs backing up? This page lists where the data lives — and warns about the places where a backup likes to quietly miss.
data.scanHint: Only reading and measuring happens here. WinZii deliberately does not copy the actual data — that belongs to a backup program, not to a tool like this one.
data.profilesHint: Size of the personal folders per account. The total is the space a full backup needs.
data.moveHint: Copies the personal folders of an account to another drive — to an external disk, not to the technician's stick. The source is left untouched: WinZii copies and deletes nothing.
data.outlookHint: PST files hold folders that exist only on this PC. OST files are merely a copy of the mailbox and are rebuilt.
data.browserHint: Saved passwords stay encrypted and cannot be taken along — the bookmarks can.
data.devicesHint: So that nothing is forgotten after a fresh install. The list is saved as geraete.json and can be recreated on the “Restore” page.
data.keysHint: These exports write passwords and keys in plain text onto the drive. That is why each one asks separately.
data.reportHint: Sums the inventory up as a printable page — the checklist for the fresh install.
